next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Build a named layout profile system accessible from the dashboard toolbar that lets users save, load, rename, and delete complete layout configurations — including which widgets are visible, their column assignments, and their vertical order. Profiles should persist to localStorage with export/import as JSON for backup and cross-device transfer. Add a dedicated mobile-optimized 'Layout' bottom sheet (slide-up panel) that consolidates the gear-button actions, visibility toggles, and profile switching into one place, replacing the need to open individual widget gear menus for bulk reorganization. The bottom sheet should be triggered by a floating action button on mobile viewports (screen width < 768px) and hidden on desktop where the existing toolbar controls suffice.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The settings button added in this mission solves per-widget reordering on mobile, but users who want to completely reorganize their layout still need to tap many individual gear menus. A profile/layout manager would let them switch between saved configurations in one tap. The mobile bottom sheet would be the natural evolution of the gear-button pattern — a consolidated UX for the use case this mission addressed.

final_report.summary: Successfully implemented a mobile-friendly widget panel settings button (⚙ gear icon) for the AtlasForge dashboard. Each widget card header now has a settings button that appears next to the collapse toggle — but ONLY when tiles are unlocked. Tapping the gear opens a fixed-position popup menu with four actions: 'Left Panel', 'Middle Panel', 'Move Up', and 'Move Down'. The currently-active panel option and boundary positions (first/last card) are automatically grayed out. All actions persist via the existing localStorage layout system. The implementation was validated with full Selenium functional tests in a live Firefox browser — 7/7 tests passed, including confirmation that gear buttons appear/hide correctly based on lock state, the popup positions correctly near screen edges, moves actually mutate the DOM, and toast notifications confirm each action to the user.
key_achievements: Added ⚙ gear settings button to all 16 widget card headers in main_bundled.html
CSS rule `body:not(.tiles-locked) .widget-settings-btn` enforces the 'unlocked only' constraint without any JS overhead
Single shared popup (#widget-settings-popup) appended to document.body to escape stacking contexts — correctly positions near screen edge with flip-up logic
Four actions fully implemented: Left Panel, Middle Panel, Move Up, Move Down — all wired to the existing drag-drop infrastructure (pushHistoryBeforeDrag, saveLayout, showToast)
Disabled state logic: current-column buttons and boundary position buttons auto-gray correctly
Mobile-optimized: 48px tap targets on coarse pointer devices, haptic feedback via navigator.vibrate, fixed positioning works across all viewports
Bundle rebuilt and deployed — both bundle.min.js and bundle.min.css updated
27/27 tests passed: 17 integration tests + 10 adversarial edge-case tests + 7 Selenium functional tests
challenges_overcome: Stacking context issue: popup was clipping behind other elements — solved by moving it to document.body in initWidgetSettingsButtons()
Popup viewport overflow on mobile: implemented flip-up logic that repositions popup above button when it would overflow bottom edge
event.stopPropagation() required on gear button clicks to prevent triggering the card collapse handler
No right panel option: right panel column is disabled in this dashboard — respected by only offering column-1 (Left) and column-2 (Middle) as targets
Selenium discovery: main_bundled.html is served directly, not from a bundle template, meaning HTML edits take effect immediately without cache invalidation
lessons_learned: CSS-only show/hide (body:not(.tiles-locked)) is more reliable than JS toggling for lock-state gating — no event wiring needed
Shared single popup (moved to body) beats per-card popup instances for both DOM cleanliness and stacking context correctness
Fixed positioning for mobile popups requires viewport overflow detection — always check both bottom and left edges
16 card headers in main_bundled.html require the settings button; mission-card is correctly excluded as it has no standard card-header structure
Selenium functional tests caught that the served HTML is main_bundled.html directly, not a compiled bundle — worth verifying serving architecture before assuming build pipeline applies
